## Summary

Adds the **Ling-3.1-flash** cookbook page (`docs/cookbook/autoregressive/InclusionAI/Ling-3.1-flash.mdx` + config/benchmark snippets + navigation), modeled on the Ling-3.0-flash page and written with the `cookbook-add-model` skill.

## What's in the page

- **Deployment cells** (verified badges): H200 TP8+EP8 + NEXTN and GB300 TP4+EP4 + NEXTN, both on `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-ling-3.1-flash`
- **Playground**: speculative options (NEXTN enabled; DSpark disabled — no compatible draft), HiCache/Mooncake L3 preset, MoE/attention/PD axes with model-specific disabled reasons
- **Advanced usage**: reasoning on/off, tool-calling round trip, HiCache with Mooncake — all with verbatim request/response captures from the current checkpoint
- **Benchmark widget**: measured speed entries (H200 bs=1 251.2 tok/s, TPOT 3.63 ms; conc 32 1640.8 tok/s/GPU) and matched accuracy controls (NEXTN 96.89% vs standard 96.97% GSM8K, stop 99.85% vs 99.77%); GB300 bs=1 180.0 tok/s
- **Acceptance-length table** in the 3.0 page's style (2.61 random / 2.43 full GSM8K / 2.13 real text)

## Verification

- `node docs/scripts/check_cookbook_configs.mjs`, pre-commit, `mint validate`, `mint broken-links`, Playwright browser smoke — all pass
- Two review rounds against `cookbook-review-pr` and `cookbook-add-model` skills; all findings addressed
- Every number on the page was measured on the current checkpoint and the `dev-ling-3.1-flash` image (day-0 code PR: branch `bailing-v3-day0`)

## Notes

- The image tag is an alias of the cu13 variant; both resolve to the same multi-arch manifest.
- Mooncake service commands and the flush_cache idle caveat come from a real L3 run (prefetch verified on all 8 TP ranks).

 ---
 title: Ling-3.0-flash-VL
 description: "Deploy Ling-3.0-flash-VL with SGLang — a ~125B hybrid KDA + MLA MoE vision-language model (5.1B active) with image and video input, thinking mode, and 128K context on Blackwell and Hopper GPUs."
-tag: NEW

 ## Deployment

@@ -0,0 +1,364 @@ +--- +title: Ling-3.1-flash +description: "Deploy Ling-3.1-flash with SGLang — FP8 hybrid KDA + MLA MoE recipes for H200 and GB300 GPUs, measured accuracy and decode speed, and Mooncake prefix caching." +tag: NEW +--- + +## Deployment + + + + + +Use the Ling-3.1-flash image, which includes model support and the decode optimizations used by these recipes. The image supports multiple CPU architectures: + +```bash Command +docker pull lmsysorg/sglang:dev-ling-3.1-flash +``` + +Select **Docker** in the command panel to launch the matching image. The **Python** command requires an environment with the same Ling-3.1-flash build. See the [installation guide](/docs/get-started/install#method-3-using-docker) for Docker setup. + + +The first launch in a fresh container spends about five extra minutes compiling JIT kernels for the speculative-decoding graphs (about 4–5 minutes once, then about 30 seconds). Mount a persistent cache volume, for example `-v ~/.cache:/root/.cache`, to skip it on later starts. + + + + +Pick your hardware to generate the launch command: + +- **Low-Latency** — single-user chat and interactive requests, with NEXTN speculative decoding. Verified on H200 and GB300; H20-3e, H800, H100, and B200 recipes are provided unverified. + +For prefix-heavy multi-turn workloads, enable **HiCache** in the Playground after starting the Mooncake services in §3.3. The combination is verified: prefix hits return from Mooncake L3 on every TP rank. + +import { Deployment } from "/src/snippets/_deployment.jsx"; +import { config } from "/src/snippets/configs/inclusionAI/ling-3.1-flash.jsx"; +import { benchmarks } from "/src/snippets/configs/inclusionAI/ling-3.1-flash-benchmarks.jsx"; + + + +## Playground + +Experiment with SGLang features on top of the selected deployment. The speculative-decoding options show the checkpoint requirements; the multi-turn prefix-cache preset adds the paired scheduler flags and environment setting. + +import { Playground } from "/src/snippets/_playground.jsx"; + + + +## 1. Model introduction + +[Ling-3.1-flash](https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/Ling-3.1-flash) is a hybrid-attention Mixture-of-Experts language model using the `BailingMoeV3ForCausalLM` architecture. Its 72 layers combine Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) with Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA), with 512 routed experts. The checkpoint uses FP8 E4M3 weights in 128×128 blocks with dynamic activation quantization. + +The model supports reasoning and structured tool calling, with a context limit of 262,144 tokens. + +**Checkpoint:** [inclusionAI/Ling-3.1-flash](https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/Ling-3.1-flash). **License:** MIT. + +The model has about 560B total parameters (512 routed experts with 8 active plus one shared expert per token, about 17B active), 72 layers, and FP8 block-quantized weights. + +## 2. Configuration tips + +- Use eight H200 GPUs with `--tp 8 --ep 8`, or four GB300 GPUs with `--tp 4 --ep 4`. SGLang detects FP8 from the checkpoint. +- On H200, enable `SGLANG_ENABLE_FP8_BLOCK_GEMV=1` and `SGLANG_ENABLE_FUSED_KDA_OUTPUT_QUANT=1`. Both are included in the generated commands; they are no-ops on GB300 (SM10x). +- Leave `--mem-fraction-static` at its default. SGLang auto-selects the `ling3` reasoning and tool-call parsers for this architecture; you can change the parser settings in the Playground. +- **NEXTN:** add `--speculative-algorithm NEXTN` for built-in MTP speculative decoding. Measured acceptance length is 2.61 on random tokens and 2.13 on real-text probes. +- For prefix-heavy, multi-turn workloads, select **Cache fork and tail** in the Playground. It combines `--mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer`, `--chunked-prefill-size 4096`, and `SGLANG_SPLIT_PREFILL_AT_MAMBA_FORK=1`. GPU checks confirmed both fork and tail states are cached, saving about 576 tokens per subsequent turn in the measured workload. + +### Playground support + +- **Attention:** BailingKDA shards its projections on attention TP; DP-attention size must divide TP. Prefill CP is disabled because BailingKDA does not implement the required sequence gather and recurrent-state handling. +- **MoE:** Auto, DeepGEMM, and Triton use the FP8 MoE runner paths. EP must divide TP. +- **PD disaggregation:** the Playground exposes separate prefill and decode roles with Mooncake transfer. The runtime has hybrid recurrent-state transfer support, but this model's PD deployment has not been verified. Provision separate workers and route requests through a PD-aware gateway; select the role-specific command for each worker. +- **HiCache:** enabling Mooncake on the H200 base preserves NEXTN and adds direct page-first I/O, hybrid-KDA prefix settings, and TCP storage endpoints. + +### Performance + +On H200 TP8 + EP8 with NEXTN and the decode gates enabled, batch-size-1 output throughput measures **251.2 tokens/s**. GB300 NEXTN batch-size-1 result: `180.0 tok/s (TPOT 5.14 ms, accept 2.59)`. + +Acceptance length is the mean number of tokens accepted per speculative verification step, including the target bonus token: + + + + + + + + + + + + + + +
WorkloadAcceptance length
Random-token benchmark (bs=1)2.61
GSM8K smoke (HiCache serve)2.29
Full GSM8K (cumulative)2.43
Real-text probes (30 prompts)2.13
+ +The image includes KDA normalization/quantization fusion, FP8 block GEMV, router-gate matrix-vector kernels, and a 512-expert top-k router. + + + +Launch the H200 **Low-Latency** recipe, then run: + +```bash Command +python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \ + --backend sglang \ + --host localhost --port 30000 \ + --model inclusionAI/Ling-3.1-flash \ + --dataset-name random \ + --random-input-len 2048 --random-output-len 512 \ + --random-range-ratio 1 \ + --num-prompts 16 --max-concurrency 1 \ + --flush-cache --seed 11 +``` + +For the concurrency-32 row in the benchmark widget: + +```bash Command +python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \ + --backend sglang \ + --host localhost --port 30000 \ + --model inclusionAI/Ling-3.1-flash \ + --dataset-name random \ + --random-input-len 4096 --random-output-len 512 \ + --random-range-ratio 1 \ + --num-prompts 96 --max-concurrency 32 \ + --flush-cache --seed 11 +``` + + + + + +```bash Command +pip install sgl-eval +sgl-eval run gsm8k \ + --base-url http://localhost:30000/v1 \ + --num-threads 32 +``` + +Evaluate all 1,319 questions and inspect completion reasons as well as accuracy. For the H200 NEXTN recipe, compare the stop rate with the measured 99.85%; accuracy alone can hide generations that reach the token limit. + + + +## 3. Advanced usage + +### 3.1 Reasoning + +The `ling3` parser returns reasoning in `message.reasoning_content` and the final answer in `message.content`. Thinking is enabled by default. To request a direct answer, pass `"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": false}` in the request body, or `extra_body={"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": False}}` with the OpenAI Python client. + + + +```python Python +from openai import OpenAI + +client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:30000/v1", api_key="EMPTY") + +response = client.chat.completions.create( + model="Ling-3.1-flash", + messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "What is 15% of 240?"}], +) +print(response.choices[0].message.reasoning_content) +print(response.choices[0].message.content) +``` + + + + + +```text Output +15% of 240 = 0.15 × 240 = 36. + +Quick check: 10% of 240 = 24, 5% = 12, total 36. Correct. +**36** + +Here's the calculation: +- 15% = 0.15 +- 0.15 × 240 = 36 + +Or break it down: 10% of 240 = 24, and 5% of 240 = 12, so 24 + 12 = **36** +``` + +The first block is `reasoning_content` (59 tokens); the second is `content`. `finish_reason` is `stop`. + + + + + +```python Python +response = client.chat.completions.create( + model="Ling-3.1-flash", + messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "What is 15% of 240?"}], + extra_body={"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": False}}, +) +print(response.choices[0].message.reasoning_content) # None +print(response.choices[0].message.content) +``` + + + + + +```text Output +None +15% of 240 is **36**. + +Calculation: +- 10% of 240 = 24 +- 5% of 240 = 12 +- 24 + 12 = **36** + +Or directly: 240 × 0.15 = **36** +``` + +`reasoning_content` is `None` and `reasoning_tokens` is 0. + + + +### 3.2 Tool calling + +The `ling3` tool-call parser returns structured calls in `message.tool_calls`, with `finish_reason` set to `tool_calls`. Send tools through the OpenAI-compatible `tools` field and return each tool result with its matching `tool_call_id`. Read both `reasoning_content` and `content` on the follow-up assistant turn. + + + +```python Python +tools = [ + { + "type": "function", + "function": { + "name": "get_weather", + "description": "Get the current weather for a city", + "parameters": { + "type": "object", + "properties": { + "city": {"type": "string", "description": "City name, e.g. Beijing"}, + "unit": {"type": "string", "enum": ["celsius", "fahrenheit"]}, + }, + "required": ["city"], + }, + }, + } +] + +import json + + +def get_weather(city: str, unit: str = "celsius"): + # Stand-in for your real tool implementation. + return {"city": city, "temperature": 22, "condition": "sunny", "unit": unit} + + +response = client.chat.completions.create( + model="Ling-3.1-flash", + messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "What's the weather like in Hangzhou right now?"}], + tools=tools, + tool_choice="required", +) +msg = response.choices[0].message +call = msg.tool_calls[0] +print(msg.model_dump_json(indent=2, exclude_none=True)) +print(response.choices[0].finish_reason) + +# Execute the tool yourself, then return its result on the matching tool_call_id +result = get_weather(**json.loads(call.function.arguments)) + +follow_up = client.chat.completions.create( + model="Ling-3.1-flash", + messages=[ + {"role": "user", "content": "What's the weather like in Hangzhou right now?"}, + msg, + {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": call.id, "content": json.dumps(result)}, + ], + tools=tools, +) +print(follow_up.choices[0].message.reasoning_content) +print(follow_up.choices[0].message.content) +``` + + + + + +```json Output +{ + "message": { + "role": "assistant", + "content": "", + "reasoning_content": "The user wants to know the current weather in Hangzhou. I'll call the get_weather function with city \"Hangzhou\". The unit parameter is optional - I'll use celsius as default since Hangzhou is in China.", + "tool_calls": [ + { + "id": "call_2bae8419df9d44f2bb54c22f", + "index": 0, + "type": "function", + "function": { + "name": "get_weather", + "arguments": "{\"city\": \"Hangzhou\", \"unit\": \"celsius\"}" + } + } + ] + }, + "finish_reason": "tool_calls" +} +``` + +The follow-up assistant turn answers with both `reasoning_content` and `content` populated. + + + +### 3.3 HiCache with Mooncake + +With HiCache enabled, prefix state is written through to Mooncake L3 and later requests prefetch it back: measured 5952 of 6000 tokens restored from storage on every TP rank. Mooncake runs as L3 prefix storage over TCP; start the metadata server, master, and storage client before launching SGLang. Run these services on the same host as the SGLang container: + + + +```bash Command +docker run --rm --network host --ipc=host \ + lmsysorg/sglang:dev-ling-3.1-flash \ + bash -lc ' + python3 -m mooncake.http_metadata_server --port 8290 & + mooncake_master --port 50171 --metrics_port 9024 & + exec mooncake_client \ + --host=127.0.0.1 \ + --port=50172 \ + --master_server_address=127.0.0.1:50171 \ + --metadata_server=http://127.0.0.1:8290/metadata \ + --protocol=tcp \ + --device_names= \ + --global_segment_size=4294967296 \ + --enable_http_server=true \ + --http_port=8291 + ' +``` + + + + + +```text Output +I1014 11:47:24.542050 328820 master.cpp:1522] Master service started on port 50171, max_threads=16, enable_metric_reporting=1, metrics_port=9024, ... +I1014 11:47:24.558478 328853 master_admin_service.cpp:301] Master Admin Metrics: role=leader, state=serving, service_ready=true, ... +I1014 11:47:27.557325 328879 real_client.cpp:1935] Client HTTP server started on port 8291 +``` + + + +Select **H200 → Low-Latency** in Deployment, then enable **HiCache → Mooncake** in the Playground. Keep NEXTN inherited from the base. Docker commands use host networking so the SGLang container can reach these localhost services. Change the master and metadata endpoints in the **Env** dialog for a remote store. + +The TCP recipe leaves `MOONCAKE_DEVICE` and `--device_names` empty. The generated command includes `extra_buffer`, direct page-first I/O, and `hicache_storage_pass_prefix_keys=true` for hybrid KDA prefix reuse. To verify L3 round-trip: send a long prompt (thousands of tokens), wait for the server to go idle, flush with `curl -X POST http://localhost:30000/flush_cache -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}'`, then repeat the same prompt. + + + +```text Output +[2026-10-14 11:59:25 TP0 EP0] HiCache prefetch success req=2619007c50024156a9872f10ec14606a completed=5952 matched=0 loaded=5952 occupied=0 +[2026-10-14 11:59:25 TP1 EP1] HiCache prefetch success req=2619007c50024156a9872f10ec14606a completed=5952 matched=0 loaded=5952 occupied=0 +[2026-10-14 11:59:25 TP2 EP2] HiCache prefetch success req=2619007c50024156a9872f10ec14606a completed=5952 matched=0 loaded=5952 occupied=0 +[2026-10-14 11:59:25 TP7 EP7] HiCache prefetch success req=2619007c50024156a9872f10ec14606a completed=5952 matched=0 loaded=5952 occupied=0 +[2026-10-14 11:59:25 TP6 EP6] HiCache prefetch success req=2619007c50024156a9872f10ec14606a completed=5952 matched=0 loaded=5952 occupied=0 +[2026-10-14 11:59:25 TP5 EP5] HiCache prefetch success req=2619007c50024156a9872f10ec14606a completed=5952 matched=0 loaded=5952 occupied=0 +[2026-10-14 11:59:25 TP4 EP4] HiCache prefetch success req=2619007c50024156a9872f10ec14606a completed=5952 matched=0 loaded=5952 occupied=0 +[2026-10-14 11:59:25 TP3 EP3] HiCache prefetch success req=2619007c50024156a9872f10ec14606a completed=5952 matched=0 loaded=5952 occupied=0 +``` + + + + +`POST /flush_cache` is refused with 400 while any request is still in flight — the L3 write-through finishes after the response returns. Wait a few seconds of idle before flushing. + + +For storage sizing and backend details, see [HiCache best practices](/docs/advanced_features/hicache_best_practices).
